description: invoices.amount_cents is nullable, but an invoice with no amount is a contradiction in terms — every row this table will ever hold needs a real amount, and Postgres will happily accept NULL there today.

required_findings.justification: amount_cents is the one column an invoice row cannot meaningfully exist without, yet it has no `not null` constraint (unlike status and created_at on the same table). A row can be inserted with amount_cents left NULL, and every downstream sum/total computation over invoices.amount_cents will then silently produce NULL or skip that row instead of failing loudly at write time.

explanation: A one-column schema defect: the table's own other required fields (workspace_id, status, created_at) are all correctly `not null`, making amount_cents's omission a clear, isolated inconsistency rather than a stylistic choice — no application code is needed to see that an invoice's amount is not optional.
